description:
FILED s412 (Fable) from a Phase C probe (docs/plan-one-compiler-s411.md; the Include-tail decline was lifted in _lower_embedded_body).  PRE-EXISTING: HEAD before Phase C (v1's parse_block_to_cl_string route) answers the same 7.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
  sub f { 7 }
  my $a = eval { f(); no warnings; };  # perl 7, PCL 7
  my @b = eval { f(); use strict; };   # perl (), PCL (7)
  my @e = do   { f(); no warnings; };  # perl (), PCL (7)
  my @d = eval { f(); require POSIX; }; # both: require's value (a tail `require` IS a runtime statement)

WHY: perl evaluates `f();` in VOID context (it is not the syntactic tail) â in list context nothing is left on the stack; in scalar context the last SV is.  PCL lowers the block as a progn whose last runtime form is f()'s call (the use/no emits no runtime form), so both contexts see 7.  Perl documents the value of a block ending in a non-expression loosely; matching it exactly means: when a block's syntactic tail is a use/no, evaluate the previous statement in VOID and yield () in list context / that value in scalar.  Rare in real code (a `no warnings` as the LAST statement of an eval/do body).  Low priority; owner = the E5.3 Include-family port (use/no/require, ~378/corpus).
subject: A block whose LAST statement is `use`/`no` (a compile-time-only statement) has NO list-context value in perl (`my @b = eval { f(); no warnings }` is empty; scalar context gives f()'s value 7) â PCL yields the previous statement's value in both contexts (7)
